title: Finite coefficient compact-support comparison respects site transport, refinement and composition
statement:
Fix a field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$ and a prime $\ell\ne p$; all schemes below are separated and of finite type over $k$, and all scheme morphisms are $k$-morphisms [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. Let $A\to B$ be a unital homomorphism of finite commutative rings annihilated by powers of $\ell$. On the small etale and pro-etale sites use ordinary constant-ring module derived categories [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules, def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. A bounded constructible finite-Tor complex means one with constructible cohomology, zero outside a finite interval, whose derived tensor with every degree-zero module sheaf has cohomology in a fixed finite interval [def-weil-pbc-etale-constructible-sheaf, def-weil-proetale-constructible-sheaf, def-weil-proetale-tor-amplitude]. Write $T_T=(-)_B=-\otimes^L_{A_T}B_T$ on either site [det-sp-scalar-extension-functor, lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback].

For a separated finite-type map $h:U\to V$ and a compactification $c=(U\xrightarrow j\bar U\xrightarrow r V)$, define $F_{h,R}^{c,\mathrm{et}}=Rr_{*,R}^{\mathrm{et}}j_{!,R}^{\mathrm{et}}$ and $F_{h,R}^c=Rr_{*,R}j_{!,R}$, for $R=A,B$ [def-amb-etale-compact-support, det-sp-reduction-direct-image]. The canonical coefficient maps $\beta_h^c:T_VF_{h,A}^{c,\mathrm{et}}\to F_{h,B}^{c,\mathrm{et}}T_U$ and $b_h^c:T_VF_{h,A}^c\to F_{h,B}^cT_U$ are the proper direct-image coefficient maps followed by the extension-by-zero tensor identifications. Here each proper map is the $B$-linear adjoint transpose of the $A$-counit after coefficient extension, as in [det-sp-reduction-direct-image].

Let $\nu_T^*$ be the exact site comparison of [lem-sf-comparison-pullback-exact] and let $\delta_{T,M}:(\nu_T^*M)_B\xrightarrow{\sim}\nu_T^*(M_B)$ be its canonical tensor comparison [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. Define $c_{h,R}^c:\nu_V^*F_{h,R}^{c,\mathrm{et}}\to F_{h,R}^c\nu_U^*$ by the counit-mate proper comparison [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image-canonical-mate] followed by the site comparison for extension by zero [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero-comparison]. This is the compact-support comparison used to transport counits in [det-sp-et-proet-adjunction-transfer]. On bounded constructible finite-Tor etale input $L$ all these coefficient and site comparisons are isomorphisms and satisfy
$$
 F_{h,B}^c(\delta_{U,L})\circ b_h^c(\nu_U^*L)\circ (c_{h,A}^c(L))_B
 =c_{h,B}^c(L_B)\circ\nu_V^*(\beta_h^c(L))\circ\delta_{V,F_{h,A}^{c,\mathrm{et}}L}.
$$
Thus transport of an etale adjunction counit through this specified $c_{h,R}^c$, with the counit formula of [det-sp-et-proet-adjunction-transfer], carries a coefficient-counit identity using $\beta_h^c$ to the same identity using the named $b_h^c$.

The coefficient maps also respect the canonical compactification refinement and composition identifications on this input class. More precisely, on the etale site let $\phi_{h,R}^{c',c}:F_{h,R}^c\xrightarrow{\sim}F_{h,R}^{c'}$ and $\alpha_{g,f,R}:F_{g,R}F_{f,R}\xrightarrow{\sim}F_{gf,R}$ be the canonical refinement and composition maps of [lem-amb-etale-compact-comparisons]; in this paragraph $F$ denotes the functor on the site under consideration. On etale-origin pro-etale objects use their counterparts through the specified $c_{h,R}^c$. These are the canonical compactification maps, and $c$ intertwines their refinement and composition identifications. For $q_h=\beta_h$ on the etale site and $q_h=b_h$ on the pro-etale site,
$$
 q_h^{c'}(L)\circ T_V(\phi_{h,A}^{c',c}(L))
 =\phi_{h,B}^{c',c}(L_B)\circ q_h^c(L),
$$
and for composable $X\xrightarrow fY\xrightarrow gZ$,
$$
 q_{gf}(L)\circ T_Z(\alpha_{g,f,A}(L))
 =\alpha_{g,f,B}(L_B)\circ F_{g,B}(q_f(L))\circ q_g(F_{f,A}L).
$$
For a separated etale morphism of finite type $e:U\to V$, let $c_{e,R}:F^{c,\mathrm{et}}_{e,R}\xrightarrow{\sim}De_{\Sigma!,R}$ be the canonical identification of the compact-support candidate with the exact etale sum extension [def-weil-pbc-etale-sum-extension] given by [lem-asd-etale-compact-support-normalization], and let $\sigma_e(L):(De_{\Sigma!,A}L)_B\xrightarrow{\sim}De_{\Sigma!,B}(L_B)$ be the summandwise tensor identification, computed on a K-flat representative of $L$. Then
$$
 c_{e,B}(L_B)\circ\beta_e^c(L)=\sigma_e(L)\circ(c_{e,A}(L))_B .
$$
The refinement square also holds for the canonical comparison through any common refinement, and the composition equality respects identities and associativity. All assertions are natural in $L$ and require no flatness or finite projective-dimension hypothesis on $B$ over $A$.

source.place: Tag 0GL6 (remark-Rf-lower-shriek-change-of-rings), canonical torsion coefficient comparison; Tag 0F7J (lemma-shriek-composition), canonical composition through compatible compactifications. The displayed site/coefficient and refinement squares are agent-stated coherence for these normalized constructions, expanding the Charts and Locality paragraphs of main-20261015 det-sp-reduction-exceptional.proof.md; neither tag alone states the site square.

proof.text: All the schemes in a compactification are Noetherian: a field is Noetherian, and finite type over it preserves Noetherianity [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]. Choose Tor bounds a<=b for L. By [lem-sf-etale-flat-constructible], represent L by a bounded complex P of flat constructible A-module sheaves in [a,b]. The finite stupid filtration of P has flat sheaves as successive shifted quotients; tensoring an acyclic complex with each quotient is acyclic, so induction over this finite filtration proves P is K-flat. The canonical derived pullback/tensor construction of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] computes coefficient extension and nu^* using these flat terms. Thus nu^*P is bounded and flat termwise; its cohomology is constructible by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-ring-constructible-derived-origin]. In particular nu^*L is in Dctf. By [det-sp-scalar-extension-functor](2), its B-extension is in Dctf, with the same Tor bounds. Monoidality identifies it with nu^*(L_B); reflection of bounded constructibility by the same finite-ring origin theorem shows that L_B is bounded constructible etale. The bounded flat model P tensor_A B also proves its etale finite Tor bound directly, since its terms are flat over B. For any finite-Tor constructible etale input E considered below, the same argument applies. No bound on the projective dimension of B over A has been used.

proof.text: Write t_j:T j_{!,A}\to j_{!,B}T for the open coefficient identification. The sheaf tensor comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-slice-extension-tensor] sends a section in an open-extension summand tensor b to that section tensor b in the same summand. Since open extension is exact on both sites [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-exact, lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero], this gives its derived comparison as well: it preserves K-flatness because j_!P tensor N=j_!(P tensor j^*N), and j^* and j_! are exact. Here j^* is restriction to the localized site. The site comparison e_j:nu^*j_!^et\to j_!^pro nu^* is the natural open-extension identification [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero-comparison]. On each summand the two orders of coefficient and site comparison both send x tensor b to nu^*x tensor b; sheafification and degreewise passage preserve this equality. Consequently j_{!,B}(delta_U)t_j(nu_U^*L)T(e_{j,A})=e_{j,B}(L_B)nu^*(t_j(L))delta_X. This proves the open version of the required square, with the named maps and their counits.

proof.text: For a proper r:W\to V, let s_R=Rr_{*,R}, l_R=r_R^*, and epsilon_R:l_Rs_R\to1 be the ordinary inverse-image/direct-image counit. Write lambda:T_W l_A \to l_B T_V for the canonical tensor/pullback isomorphism. By the normalization in [det-sp-reduction-direct-image] the coefficient map q_r:T_Vs_A\to s_BT_W is uniquely determined by epsilon_B(T_W E) l_B(q_r(E)) lambda_{s_AE}=T_W(epsilon_A(E)). Write a_R:nu_W^*l_R^et\to l_R^pro nu_V^* for the specified comparison [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback]. The site map d_{r,R} has the equally specified equation epsilon_R^pro(nu_W^*E) l_R^pro(d_{r,R}(E)) a_{R,s_R^et E}=nu_W^*(epsilon_R^et(E)), and is invertible on D^+ by [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image-canonical-mate]. These equations specify actual morphisms, not chosen endpoint isomorphisms. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting](1),(2) to the rectangle with the two coefficient squares and the two site squares. The two left-adjoint pastings coincide: all four pullbacks act on the same underlying inverse images and the tensor identifications only reassociate a tensor x tensor a tensor b, sending it to x tensor ab. This can be computed on K-flat resolutions by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. Equality of their mates therefore gives s_B^pro(delta_W) q_r^pro(nu_W^*E) T_V(d_{r,A}(E))=d_{r,B}(E_B)nu_V^*(q_r^et(E))delta_V for every E such that E and E_B are bounded below. This is the domain of both cited direct-image site mates. All applications here have E=j_!L or a bounded constructible finite-Tor input produced below: Step 2 preserves finite Tor amplitude under j_!, and Step 1 gives boundedness after scalar extension. Merely assuming E bounded below would not suffice when A\to B is nonflat. This equality itself does not require q_r to be invertible.

proof.text: For h=rj, expand c_{h,R} as s_R^pro(e_{j,R}) d_{r,R}(j_!^et-), and q_h as s_B(t_j)q_r(j_{!,A}-). Substitute the proper equality of Step 3 and the open equality of Step 2; naturality of d_r and q_r moves their whiskered e_j and t_j to the right. The resulting equality is precisely F_{h,B}(delta_U)b_h(nu_U^*L)T_V(c_{h,A}(L))=c_{h,B}(L_B)nu_V^*(beta_h(L))delta_V. Both constituents of c are invertible, by the canonical proper mate theorem and the extension-zero comparison. First apply [det-sp-reduction-direct-image] to the identity coefficient map A\to A: its assertion that the comparison lies in Dctf shows that F_{h,A} nu_U^*L is Dctf. Apply it to B\to B and L_B to obtain the same assertion over B. Now its A\to B comparison b_h is invertible on nu_U^*L, with both sides in Dctf. The displayed square now implies that nu_V^*beta_h is invertible. The source and target of beta_h are bounded below: their site pullbacks are isomorphic, via the square and c, to the Dctf objects just obtained; exactness of nu^* identifies cohomology, and full faithfulness on sheaves reflects vanishing. Full faithfulness on D^+ [thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison] then reflects invertibility of beta_h. Indeed lift the inverse by fullness and check the two inverse identities by faithfulness. The finite-ring origin theorem also reflects bounded constructibility of F_h^et L from F_h^pro nu^*L; finite Tor amplitude reflects by testing against etale module sheaves and using monoidality and faithful exact comparison. Thus composition inputs F_f^et L and their pro-etale counterparts remain in the required class.

proof.text: The same transpose calculation controls the building blocks of refinement and composition. For proper maps r followed by p, take the inverse transpose of the coefficient map for R(pr)_*, using the composite ordinary adjunction. At E its counit is the composite r_A^*p_A^*s_{p,A}s_{r,A}E \to r_A^*s_{r,A}E \to E, first r_A^*(epsilon_{p,A}(s_{r,A}E)) and then epsilon_{r,A}(E); hence the transpose of the composite s_{p,B}(q_r)q_p(s_{r,A}-) is T(epsilon_r r^*epsilon_p), which is also the transpose defining q_{pr}. Injectivity of the adjunction bijection gives q_{pr}=s_{p,B}(q_r)q_p(s_{r,A}-), after the canonical direct-image compositors [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition]. This is [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting](2) for the coefficient squares. It applies on either site and also to the site squares. For composable open immersions j_1,j_2, [lem-cbc-extension-zero-composition] identifies j_{2!}j_{1!} with (j_2j_1)_!. Starting with a section x tensor b in the nested extension summand, successive t_{j_2} and j_{2!}(t_{j_1}) put x tensor b in its composite summand; t_{j_2j_1} puts exactly the same section in that summand. The maps agree before sheafification and on the bounded flat complexes of Step 1, so they agree after derived descent. This gives the open-composition coefficient equation, and replacing x tensor b by nu^*x gives the site-composition equation. Identity maps give identity comparisons by the triangle identities, equivalently clause (4) of mate pasting.

proof.text: For the cartesian proper/open square in the composition tower, apply [lem-sp-proper-open-coefficient-mate]. Its coefficient equation commutes T past the specified Gamma; its site equation intertwines that same open-adjunction map with the canonical direct-image and open-extension comparisons. For the noncartesian refinement square, apply [lem-sp-refinement-coefficient-mate] to u,j_1,j_2. Its alpha_u is exactly the specified refinement map: the open adjunct of the inverse of the three-constituent theta_u. Both equations there therefore apply to the actual refinement map. Step 1 and the finite-Tor arguments of Steps 2 and 4 supply bounded-below input and bounded-below scalar extension in all uses. These are the two building-block squares required in Steps 7--9; no cartesian characterization is applied to a noncartesian refinement.

source.place: Tags 0F7B, 0F7C, 0F7D (proper/open maps and their pasting); coefficient and site mate calculation

proof.text: Use the normalized scalar-coherence refinement clause of [lem-pur-etale-compact-scalar-coherence], which proves the proper-composition and common-refinement calculation described here. Its open normalization identifies the inverse of ExceptionalCoefficients.openIso with properOpenCoefficientOpenInverse. Equality of inverse isomorphisms therefore identifies its compactScalarMap with the specified etaleCoefficientMap. The schemes are Noetherian because they are finite type over a field. The lower bound for the actual scalar extension is supplied by Step 4. Apply the refinement clause to obtain the etale equation. For the pro-etale equation, apply Step 4 to c and d, map the etale refinement equation by exact site comparison, and use naturality of delta on the canonical etale compactification comparison. Precompose with the scalar extension of the inverse c-site comparison. Substitute the two site/coefficient squares and cancel the inverse/hom pairs. The remaining maps are definitionally the two siteRefinement maps. This proves the specified canonical comparison, including the common-refinement independence already contained in the normalized etale refinement clause.

source.place: Tag 0F7I, lemma-shriek-well-defined; explicit refinement and common-refinement calculation

proof.text: Choose a compatible compactification tower for f and g [lem-cbc-compactifiable-compatible-tower]: Y\to Ybar is open i, Ybar\to Z is proper q, X\to U is open j, U\to Xbar is open k, and p:Xbar\to Ybar is proper, with r:U\to Y proper and pk=ir cartesian. For R=A,B the ordered composite is Rq_{*,R}i_{!,R}Rr_{*,R}j_{!,R}, while the composite-map model is R(qp)_{*,R}(kj)_{!,R}. Their composition identification is the paste of Rq_*(gamma_R)j_! and the proper/open compositors. Step 6 commutes T past gamma; Step 5 commutes it past the compositors. The outer boundary of this pasted diagram is exactly q_{gf}T(alpha_{g,f,A})=alpha_{g,f,B}F_{g,B}(q_f)q_g(F_{f,A}-). This identifies the actual coefficient map q_{gf}, since its proper/open definition is the upper-right boundary, rather than defining a replacement q_{gf} by the lower-left boundary. The canonical choice independence and associativity of alpha are supplied by [lem-amb-etale-compact-comparisons]; Step 7 passes the equation to the fixed compactifications. Pasting an identity adds only identities (Step 5), and the two three-map pastings have the same outer boundary, by the horizontal and vertical coherence laws in [lem-cbc-proper-open-interchange-coherence]. This proves the identity and associativity assertions.

source.place: Tag 0F7J, lemma-shriek-composition: compatible tower and its four displayed identifications

proof.text: Apply the site version of Steps 5 and 6 to the same tower. It states that c_{gf,R}nu^*(alpha_R) equals alpha_R^pro F_g^pro(c_{f,R}) c_{g,R}(F_f^et-), with the source/target site identifications inserted. Together with the last sentence of Step 7 this proves that the specified c intertwines refinement and composition. On etale-origin objects the pro-etale counterparts in the statement are precisely these transported maps. Substitute the site/coefficient square of Step 4 into the etale refinement equation of Step 7 and cancel the invertible c and delta: the remaining equation is the pro-etale refinement equation with b. Doing the same on the tower equation of Step 8 cancels its intermediate c_f and c_g and yields b_{gf}T(alpha_A)=alpha_B F_{g,B}(b_f)b_g(F_{f,A}-). Naturalness ensures that each cancellation is at the same input complex. Hence the equations hold for the named pro-etale b, and the same cancellation proves common-refinement, identity and associativity compatibility.

proof.text: For separated etale e and c=(j,r), [lem-asd-etale-compact-support-normalization] identifies Rr_*j_! with exact sum extension and sends a properly supported section to its labelled sheet components. On every degree-zero sheaf H this implies R^a r_*j_!H=0 for a>0. Let P be the bounded flat model of Step 1. The slice tensor identity [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-slice-extension-tensor], exact sum extension [lem-amb-etale-adjoint-locality], and exact inverse image [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact] show e_!P is flat termwise and K-flat: tensoring with an acyclic N gives e_!(P tensor e^*N), which is acyclic. Step 2 gives flatness of j_!P. The sheaf normalization identifies r_*j_!P with e_!P termwise; it gives acyclicity also for j_!(P tensor B). Thus [lem-sp-acyclic-flat-proper-coefficient-model] applies to C=j_!P and identifies the proper coefficient map with its sheaf projection map. Compose with the open tensor identification of Step 2. On each summand the resulting map sends (x_s)_s tensor b to (x_s tensor b)_s, while both sheaf normalizations retain the sheet label s. The two routes therefore agree as maps of the representing complexes. This proves c_{e,B}(L_B) beta_e^c(L)=sigma_e(L) T(c_{e,A}(L)). The stalk description [lem-amb-etale-sum-stalks] includes empty fibres; no finiteness of the set of lifts on every test object is assumed.

proof.text: Finally the counit-transport implication is a substitution, valid whenever an etale adjunction counit is transported by the stated formula. This does not require invoking an admissibility theorem for arbitrary finite rings. Write C_R=c_{h,R}, and let a:T_U H_A \to H_B T_V be a right-functor comparison with etale identity epsilon_B^et F_B^et(a)=T_V(epsilon_A^et)(beta_h(H_A-))^{-1}. The transported counit is nu_V^*(epsilon_R^et)C_R^{-1}, by the formula specified in the statement. Solve Step 4's square for b_h^{-1}: T_V(C_A)^{-1} b_h^{-1}=delta_V^{-1}nu_V^*(beta_h^{-1})C_B^{-1}F_{h,B}(delta_U), at the indicated H_A input. Substitute this into T_V(nu_V^*epsilon_A^et C_A^{-1})b_h^{-1}. Naturality of delta moves T_V(nu^*epsilon_A^et)delta^{-1} to delta^{-1}nu^*(T_V epsilon_A^et); the etale identity then replaces T_V epsilon_A^et beta_h^{-1} by epsilon_B^et F_B^et(a). Naturality of C_B moves nu^*F_B^et(a) across C_B^{-1}. The result is the transported B-counit followed by F_{h,B} of the transported comparison a, which is exactly the coefficient-counit identity with b_h. Every comparison used above is natural, either by its cited statement or as an adjunct of a natural map, so all equations are natural in L. The coefficient change A\to B was arbitrary throughout; all uses of derived tensor were on K-flat models or by its canonical pullback comparison. The Lean counit proof isolates the categorical transport calculation: apply the site/coefficient square at HA(N), naturality of the B compact-support site comparison on a (viewed in D+), site pullback of the assumed etale counit identity, and naturality of delta at the A-counit; cancel the scalar image of the inverse A-site comparison and the hom/inv pairs. Naturality of the coefficient map is proved directly: transpose the open inverse under the B-open adjunction, use naturality of the A-open unit and scalar/pullback inverse, pass to inverse isomorphisms, and compose with naturality of scalarMate.
